title: Standing Deity (Vishnu?)

image.credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Gift of R.A. Lovell Jr.,1965
image.license: Public domain. Released under Creative Commons Zero (CC0) through the Met's Open Access program

altText: A small bronze figure of a standing deity, shown upright and facing forward. The dark metal figure is slim and about as tall as a hand held sideways.

source.verifiedBy: Met Collection API object record (title, date, medium, culture, classification, tags, public-domain flag, image URLs, credit line) and the Met catalog page (period and dimensions)

context: A small bronze figure from Sumatra, Indonesia, made in the Srivijaya period, in the 8th or 9th century. The Met's title carries a question mark because the identification as the Hindu god Vishnu is not certain. It is about 21.6 cm tall.

descriptions.k: This small bronze statue shows a god standing tall. It was made on the island of Sumatra long ago. It is thin and dark, and it faces you. Look for what the figure might be holding or wearing. What do you see?
descriptions.g12: This statue shows a god standing straight. It was made of bronze on the island of Sumatra, in Indonesia, over a thousand years ago. The title has a question mark because experts are not sure it is Vishnu. Look closely for clues. What might the figure wear or hold?
descriptions.g35: Long ago, the island of Sumatra was part of a powerful trading kingdom called Srivijaya. This bronze god, about 21 centimeters tall, was made there in the 8th or 9th century. Its title says 'Vishnu?' because scholars are not sure who it is. A question mark means the evidence is not complete. What clues could help you decide who the figure is?
descriptions.g68: Made in Sumatra during the Srivijaya period, this bronze stands only about 21.6 cm tall. The Met titles it 'Standing Deity (Vishnu?)', a reminder that identifying figures depends on attributes that can be worn or missing over time. Sculpture like this shows how Hindu ideas traveled across the sea to Southeast Asia. What clues would you look for to identify a deity, and why might a museum keep the question mark?
descriptions.g910: This bronze from Srivijaya-period Sumatra presents a standing deity whose identification as Vishnu is tentative, as the Met's question mark shows. Upright posture and frontal presentation give the figure a formal, devotional character, while its modest height of about 21.6 cm suggests an object for a shrine or private setting, though the record does not say. How does uncertainty about identity change how we look, and what can form alone tell us?
descriptions.g1112: The Met's title, 'Standing Deity (Vishnu?)', is a candid statement about the limits of identification. This 8th-9th century bronze from Sumatra belongs to the era of Srivijaya, a maritime power linked to Indian religious and artistic ideas, yet it also reflects local craft. Because the record does not describe its attributes or original setting, any iconographic claim should stay provisional. Consider how scholars weigh posture, attributes, and comparison, and what is lost when a museum label settles uncertainty too quickly.

g1112.color: How do patina and corrosion complicate our perception of the original surface, and what should we avoid assuming about it?

g1112.meaning: The Met's question mark suggests uncertainty about Vishnu. How should interpreters weigh iconographic conventions against regional variation?
g1112.culture: How does Srivijaya's position in maritime trade complicate a simple model of Indian influence, and what role did local artists and patrons play?

safety.method: Image viewed and approved by the site owner (visual review) on 2026-10-18. Earlier metadata screening: Title, classification (Sculpture), medium (Bronze), culture, and tags (Vishnu, Hinduism) checked against the museum record. The catalog page offers no label text about the figure's attributes, so descriptions stay general and avoid claims about clothing or held objects. Bare-chested depiction could not be ruled out from metadata alone.

teacherNote.context: A small bronze of a standing deity, tentatively identified by the Met as Vishnu, from Sumatra in the Srivijaya period (8th-9th century). It is about 21.6 cm tall.
directions: Have students list what a museum would need to know to remove the question mark in the title.
Discuss how religious ideas and images travel along trade routes.
Ask students to sketch a figure that can be recognized from posture alone, then explain what clues they used.
